drafted: 2026-10-29: fix sites read from the fixture source (NodeGoat's own 'Fix for' markers and the vulnerable statements); every quote checked by eval.devbench.check_keys. Needs a labeler's sign-off before any score from it is quoted as more than draft dev evidence.

keys.name: Server-Side JS Injection via eval()

fix_sites.why: eval() of req.body.preTax/afterTax/roth (lines 32-34) runs attacker JavaScript on the server; the commented fix at 36-41 (same function) replaces eval with parseInt.

keys.notes: Single site: the three eval() calls plus the adjacent commented 'Fix for A1 -1' block (36-41).

keys.name: NoSQL Injection via $where operator

fix_sites.why: The unsanitised threshold (req.query.threshold via allocations.js) is interpolated into a $where JavaScript expression; the commented fix at 63-76 parses and range-checks it first.

keys.notes: Judgement: function is the innermost named function 'searchCriteria' (line 60), as Joern also names it (eval/tests/test_names.py); the outer DAO method is getByUserIdAndThreshold (line 57). A finding that names only getByUserIdAndThreshold and gives no line in 68-88 will NOT match; add a second function if that should count. The query executes at line 86 (allocationsCol.find(searchCriteria())), inside the window. The commented fix block starts at line 63, so 63-67 lie outside the window. allocations.html:17 carries a UX-only 'Fix for A1 - 2' input-validation marker; not a server fix site. CWE-94 is listed because the marker says the input lets attackers 'inject arbitrary javascript code' into the query; CWE-89 is redundant with CWE-943 under eval/cwe.py's family rule but harmless.

keys.name: Log Injection (CRLF forging)

fix_sites.quote: console.log("Error: attempt to login with invalid user: ", userName);
fix_sites.why: The raw req.body userName is written to the log on a failed login, so CR/LF in it forges log lines; the commented fix at 66-80 encodes it or replaces CR/LF.

keys.notes: Judgement: end_line NOT extended over the 'Fix for A1 - 3' comment block (66-80) so the window (54-74) does not overlap A2-2's enumeration site (85-97). The line is inside an anonymous (err, user) => callback passed to userDAO.validateLogin; 'handleLoginRequest' is the nearest NAMED enclosing function. A1-3, A2-1 and A2-2 all have a site whose function is handleLoginRequest, so a finding naming that function matches all three at L1 regardless of line (L2/CWE separates them). No other console.log in app/routes or app/data logs user input (grep).

keys.name: Broken Auth — insecure session management

fix_sites.why: express-session is configured with only secret/saveUninitialized/resave: no cookie httpOnly, secure or maxAge and the default cookie name; the commented fixes inside the call (86-90 cookie name, 92-100 httpOnly cookie) are where a fix goes.
On login the existing session id is reused (no req.session.regenerate), i.e. session fixation; the comment block at 104-115 describes wrapping these two lines in regenerate().

keys.notes: Judgement calls: (1) the server.js site is the whole session() statement (25 lines, longer than the 1-15 norm) because both commented fixes sit inside it; its window (68-112) overlaps A8's server.js site (107-112) and A5's (42-64, window to 74), so server.js findings in 68-122 rely on L2/CWE to pick the right key. (2) The cookie block at 92-100 is marked 'Fix for A3 - XSS' and the cookie-name block at 86-90 'Fix for A5 - Security MisConfig' in the source, but GROUND_TRUTH's A2-1 keywords (httponly, cookie name, secure flag, session secret) put them here, so they are NOT in A3/A5. (3) The marker 'Fix for A2-1' in user-dao.js (plaintext password storage) is NOT here; it is under A2-2 (see there). (4) The session secret value is hard-coded in config/env/all.js:8 (cookieSecret: "session_cookie_secret_key_here"); not added as a site (GROUND_TRUTH files are server.js/session.js, and a window there would also cover cryptoKey at line 9); server.js:82 (secret: cookieSecret) is inside site 1. (5) Plain-HTTP serving (server.js:144-147) is not added. (6) Primary CWE-384 because NodeGoat's A2 tutorial cites it; the cookie-flag issues are CWE-1004 / CWE-614 / CWE-613. Site 2's line is inside the anonymous validateLogin callback; handleLoginRequest is the nearest named function (shared with A1-3 and A2-2).

keys.name: Broken Auth — weak password policy + user enumeration

fix_sites.why: Signup accepts any 1-20 character password; the commented fix at 145-149 requires 8+ chars with digits, lower and upper case.
Login renders 'Invalid username' (85) vs 'Invalid password' (94), enumerating valid user names; the commented fixes at 86-87 and 95-96 use one generic errorMessage.
The password is stored in plain text; the commented fix at 26-30 stores a bcrypt hash.
Login compares the plaintext password directly; the commented fix at 62-66 uses bcrypt.compareSync, the counterpart of the hashed storage.

keys.notes: Judgement call (largest one): the two user-dao.js sites (plaintext storage + comparison) are marked 'Fix for A2-1' / 'Fix for A2-Broken Auth' in the source and NodeGoat's tutorial puts password storage under 'A2 - 1 Session Management', but GROUND_TRUTH lists user-dao.js only under A2-2 and its A2-2 keywords include plaintext password / password hashing / comparepassword / bcrypt, so they are placed here. Drop them if A2-2 should be only password policy + enumeration (the item's name). The enumeration's error flags originate in user-dao.js validateUserDoc (78-87), but the fix the source marks is in session.js, so validateUserDoc is not a site (line 75 still falls inside the comparePassword window 51-76). Site 2's line is inside the anonymous validateLogin callback; handleLoginRequest is the nearest named function (shared with A1-3, A2-1). The PASS_RE line's error text (172-173) claims '8 to 18 characters' but the regex is /^.{1,20}$/.

keys.name: Cross-Site Scripting (auto-escaping disabled)

fix_sites.why: swig.setDefaults turns template auto-escaping off for every view; the commented fix at 138-141 (inside the same call) sets autoescape: true.

keys.notes: Site is the swig.setDefaults option (call spans 135-142, window 127-151). Not included: the httpOnly cookie block server.js:92-100 (marked 'Fix for A3 - XSS' and listed by the A3 tutorial as a second measure) is assigned to A2-1 per GROUND_TRUTH keywords; profile.js:28 (encodeForHTML of doc.website used in a URL context, a '@TODO @FIXME' the A3 tutorial points to) is a separate context-encoding XSS not among the 15; memos.html:31 ({{ marked(doc.memo) }}) and research.js:25 (res.write(body) of a fetched page) are other XSS-shaped outputs not among the 15. Findings at those places will be unmatched under this key set.

keys.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference

fix_sites.why: userId is taken from req.params (line 18: '} = req.params;') and passed to the DAO with no ownership check; the commented fix at 12-15 takes it from req.session.

keys.notes: The route that exposes the parameter is index.js:63 (app.get("/allocations/:userId", ...)); not added because the marked fix is in allocations.js. Note an IDOR finding citing index.js:63 falls inside A10's index.js window (62-82) and, if it names function 'index', matches A7/A10 by function at L1. Quote is the literal first line of the destructuring statement (16-18).

fix_sites.why: Absent control: the Helmet/nosniff middleware (x-powered-by removal, frameguard, noCache, CSP, HSTS, nosniff) is commented out in the block 38-65 ('Fix for A5 - Security MisConfig'); this is where it is wired.
The helmet (line 10) and dont-sniff-mimetype (line 14) requires are commented out; a fix re-enables both.

keys.notes: Absent control: the sites are where the middleware is (commented-out) wired, not a vulnerable statement. Site 1 is 23 lines (the whole disabled block minus the comment delimiters). Site 2's range includes three unrelated requires (11-13). Overlap: site 2's window (0-24) covers the commented csurf require at line 7 (A8 site), and site 1's window (32-74) reaches into A2-1's session site; L2 separates them. Not included: the 'Fix for A5' cookie-name block 86-90 (assigned to A2-1 per GROUND_TRUTH keywords) and the 'Fix for A5' TODO at 119-121 (static assets after session), which is not about Helmet headers. Primary CWE-693 (protection mechanism failure); CWE-16 is a category (kept as an accepted alternate because tools emit it); CWE-1021 covers the missing frameguard.

keys.notes: known_gap item. The package was identified from package.json plus the in-repo A9 tutorial, not from a CVE feed (nothing here confirms a CVE id). Other exact-pinned old versions in package.json (bcrypt-nodejs 0.0.3 line 8, needle 2.2.4 line 19, node-esapi 0.0.1 line 20) and swig ^1.4.2 (line 22) are NOT added: nothing in the repo says they are vulnerable. package.json:25-27 has a comments entry 'a9 insecure components'.
